topics: fallback and routing playbook (hosted vs dedicated)
transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2026-11-02
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Sasha Kim (Redwood AE), Miguel Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Redwood Solutions), Jules Park (Aperture Head of Alliances), Ava Mitchell (Aperture VP Sales), Marco Giannetti (Aperture Solutions Architect), Riya Narang (Aperture Channel Ops)
Links shared: https://redwood.app/share/co-sell-playbook, https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/joint-pricing-starter

Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be rough): Quick triage of top accounts, discuss fallback strategy when Dedicated capacity is constrained, agreement to run a pilot and share pricing. Some audio garble at 00:45.

[00:00] Sasha Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick roll call, then we'll dive into account mapping and the starter pricing. Jules, you on?
[00:18] Jules Park: Yeah thanks Sasha, here. Ava here as well. Marco and Riya on too.
[00:24] Miguel Ortega: Hey all, Miguel from Redwood SE. I'll run the baseline tests and be the tech point.
[00:30] Ava Mitchell: Great, let's go. We wanna move fast on this pilot if we can.
[00:45] Sasha Kim: Cool, high level — Aperture has three target accounts you mentioned in the pre-read. We're thinking a 6-week pilot, canary into production for one account, two more for pipeline motion. Main risk we see is capacity alignment if traffic spikes, and also legal asks around data residency.
[01:12] Marco Giannetti: Right yeah, data residency is a must for account two, they need EU region only and KMS integration. You mentioned Redwood Private earlier — is that still the right path?
[01:40] Miguel Ortega: For EU-only residency we can use Redwood Private or Dedicated with VPC peering, depends on customer's infra preferences. There was a note in the doc about on-prem for fully air-gapped customers, which we can support but it's higher overhead.
[02:10] Riya Narang: Question about logging — do we provide per-tenant audit logs or is it merged at org level? Compliance team needs that to be separate.
[02:35] Priya Shah: We emit token-level traces and audit logs per tenant, but retention is configurable. We'll pass the security pack. Note: audit log retention add-on is billable.
[03:05] Jules Park: On pricing — Aperture was thinking of a blended committed rate for the pilot and then per-token after. Can we get a starter SOW for a 6-week pilot with a committed block?
[03:30] Sasha Kim: Yes, we'll put together a 6-week SOW template. I'll attach a joint pricing spreadsheet — it's a starter so we can tune it after initial usage.
[04:02] Ava Mitchell: Also need to understand failure modes — if we hit Dedicated capacity limit, what's the fallback? We can't have live calls failing.
[04:30] Miguel Ortega: We've proposed a multi-tier fallback: prefer Dedicated for latency-critical calls, then fallback to a slightly higher-latency hosted variant in the same region. For really constrained situations we can route to a smaller model variant or enable KV prefix caching to reduce token cost. There's a risk of slight quality variance on fallback — we should document that in the playbook.
[05:00] Sasha Kim: Right, and we'll include a 'graceful degradation' appendix showing expected latency delta and quality regression examples for the fallbacks.
[05:30] Marco Giannetti: Can you capture specific latency numbers — we need P50 and P95 for 2k and 8k sequence lengths.
[05:55] Miguel Ortega: Absolutely. I'll run baselines on both and share results in the shared sheet. FYI our runtimes are optimized for continuous batching so numbers vary with traffic shape.
[06:20] Ava Mitchell: For the joint go-to-market motion — Aperture will bring the contact at ACME Corp. We want a co-branded joint-deck and one-pager to give to their CTO. Do you have a template?
[06:40] Sasha Kim: Yes, we have a co-sell deck template. I'll share a draft and Miguel can help with the technical slide.
[07:05] Jules Park: Stakeholders: Aperture's Deal Owner is Mara Lee, Aperture Legal will need SOC 2 attestation and SAML SSO details. Any gotchas there?
[07:30] Priya Shah: We'll share our SOC 2 report and SAML integration doc. For SSO we support SAML and OIDC; if a customer requires SCIM provisioning we can add that to the SOW.
[08:12] Riya Narang: Timeline question — if we sign the pilot SOW end of this week, when can we start benchmarks?
[08:30] Sasha Kim: Pilot testing can kick in as early as next Monday provided we have infra approvals. Miguel, is that realistic?
[08:45] Miguel Ortega: Yes, assuming we have account creds and sample prompts. I'll need a 48-hour window to provision test endpoints and run the first runs.
[09:10] Marco Giannetti: For the prompts, we're bringing in some real customer prompts — but we may sanitize PII. Will that affect the KV caching measurements?
[09:35] Miguel Ortega: If you sanitize, prefix cache hits may be lower. We'll note that in the report; ideally we test on representative production-like prompts.
[10:12] Sasha Kim: Quick note on competitive positioning — ACME's infra team evaluated CloudAI Solutions and MegaServe. Aperture's differentiator is the integration layer and go-to-market, ours is performance and observability. We should lead with a latency/cost comparison in the deck.
[11:00] Ava Mitchell: Agree; show the cost per 1k tokens with and without caching, and some annotated callouts for expected SLOs.
[12:00] Sasha Kim: On SLAs, we offer tiered options — but for pilots we usually do best-effort with low-latency targets, then upgrade to a formal SLA on Dedicated buys.
[13:05] Jules Park: Legal will want to see indemnities and data handling clauses. Who on Redwood legal should we engage?
[13:30] Sasha Kim: I'll intro Lucy Patel from Redwood legal; she'll handle the SOW/legal redlines.
[14:10] Riya Narang: Are there any special reseller margin expectations? Aperture typically expects 20% margin on top of list price.
[14:30] Sasha Kim: We'll propose a partner margin in the sheet; it's adjustable. For enterprise deals we can do bespoke partner economics.
[15:05] Miguel Ortega: Back to fallback routing — also recommend a region-level routing policy: if region A is out of capacity route to region A-alt in same geo, otherwise to hosted. That reduces cross-region data residency risk if we restrict to same geo.
[16:00] Marco Giannetti: If we route to a hosted variant in a different region, does that break data residency agreements?
[16:20] Priya Shah: It can; we'll need to enforce region constraints in routing to preserve residency, else the customer must accept a limited fallback list.
[17:05] Jules Park: For executive alignment, Mara wants a 30-min sync next Tuesday. Can we make space on your calendars?
[17:25] Sasha Kim: Yes, let's tentatively penciled for next Tue 16:00 UTC. I'll send the calendar invite after the call.
[18:30] Ava Mitchell: Anything else on the tech side? Are there any feature gaps that would block the pilot?
[18:55] Miguel Ortega: No blockers. Two asks: customer wants KMS integration and a per-tenant audit log export. Both feasible; KMS is standard integration and we can show an implementation plan.
[20:00] Riya Narang: Onboarding tasks — who will own the account handoff after the pilot?
[20:20] Sasha Kim: Post-pilot handoff usually to our CSM for onboarding; for co-sell we'll keep a joint account plan with Aperture AE and Redwood AE.
[22:00] Marco Giannetti: Any expected changes to model quality when moving from dedicated to hosted? We need to set expectations for the customer.
[22:30] Miguel Ortega: There may be tokenization or quantization differences if we use quantized hosted variants. We'll include sample outputs in the playbook comparing Dedicated vs hosted variants.
[25:00] Sasha Kim: Let's review the immediate next steps — Miguel to run the benchmarks (P50/P95 for 2k/8k), Sasha to send pricing and SOW template, Jules to confirm target accounts and introduce AEs, Priya to draft fallback routing policy.
[26:30] Jules Park: I'll aim to send the contact intros by Monday EOD.
[28:00] Ava Mitchell: For the co-branded deck, can you include a slide on support model and escalation path?
[28:20] Sasha Kim: Yes, we'll include escalation paths and contacts.
[30:00] Miguel Ortega: I'll attach a sample benchmark sheet once runs complete. Note that running 8k sequences consumes a lot of tokens so plan for cost on the pilot budget.
[31:10] Riya Narang: Regarding cost — Aperture wants a clear break down of dedicated commit vs overage vs hosted fallback. We want one line in the SOW that spells it out.
[31:40] Sasha Kim: Noted. We'll add a pricing annex to the SOW with clear commit, overage, and fallback rates.
[32:00] Marco Giannetti: Security question — do you support customer-managed keys in the private deployment? KMS with HSM?
[32:30] Priya Shah: Yes, we support customer KMS and HSM integrations for Private and Dedicated depending on contract. We'll add the KMS integration doc link.
[34:00] Sasha Kim: A couple intangibles — success criteria for the pilot: (1) latency P95 under X ms for key flows, (2) accuracy/quality metric above baseline on our eval set, (3) joint deck delivered and exec intro completed.
[35:40] Ava Mitchell: That sounds good. Let's make sure we have a quick success rubric so execs can sign off.
[36:50] Miguel Ortega: Last tech note — we'll measure warm and cold cache P95; caching will be important for cost and latency so we'll instrument token-level traces.
[38:10] Jules Park: One more ask — can Redwood provide a short note on rollback/fallback SLAs so our ops team understands expected behavior?
[38:45] Sasha Kim: Yes, the playbook will include a rollback and fallback SLA summary.
[40:15] Marco Giannetti: Any legal constraints on sharing the benchmarks publicly if we want to use them in the co-branded deck?
[40:45] Sasha Kim: We'll set them as co-marketing with Aperture approval. We'll include a clause in the SOW.
[43:00] Riya Narang: Timing on the joint exec — you mentioned next Tue for a 30-min sync. We need an agenda: 1) Pilot scope 2) timeline 3) ask 4) legal/ops checklist.
[44:00] Sasha Kim: Perfect. I'll send a proposed agenda with the invite.
[45:30] Miguel Ortega: I'll share the initial benchmark spreadsheet and work with Marco on the prompt corpus.
[47:00] Jules Park: Thanks everyone. Appreciate the speed here.
[48:02] Ava Mitchell: Quick PS — Aperture's procurement will need vendor paperwork; we can start that in parallel.
[49:10] Sasha Kim: I'll drop Redwood vendor packet and Lucy from legal on the thread.
[50:00] Marco Giannetti: One small thing — can we get an example of canary deploy policies? How do you switch traffic back if hosted fallback underperforms?
[50:30] Priya Shah: We'll include automatic rollback rules and manual override steps in the playbook. Canary is percentage-based ramp with automatic health checks.
[51:10] Sasha Kim: Ok, recap of next steps and owners, will send notes and invite. Thanks all.
[51:50] Jules Park: Thanks, bye.

Action Items (auto): Miguel to run benchmarks; Sasha to share pricing and SOW; Jules to intro accounts; Priya to draft fallback policy.

End of transcript.
